questions.question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.
A snake in the grass
options: A man with a straightforward attitude
questions.solution: A)A snake in the grass(idiom) – A secret or hidden enemy छिपा हुआ दुश्मन

questions.question:

questions.solution: B) In leaps and bounds (idiom) – Progressing very quicklyबहुत तेजी से प्रगति करना

questions.question:

questions.question:

questions.solution: C)A hard nut to crack(idiom) – Someone who is difficult to deal with जिससे निपटना मुश्किल है

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate idiomatic expression that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.
He wanted to be a professional basketball player but given his height, luck was against him
options: his health was not in his favour
the cards were stacked against him
questions.solution:
D)luck was against him'के बदले 'the cards were stacked against him' का प्रयोग होगा क्योंकि यह idiomatic expression बताता है कि किसी की परिस्थितियाँ या हालात उसके खिलाफ हैं; जैसे— Despite his hard work, the cards were stacked against him in the competition.
'the cards were stacked against him' will be used instead of 'luck was against him' because this idiomatic expression means that someone's circumstances or conditions are against them; Like— Despite his hard work, the cards were stacked against him in the competition.
